A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ScaleGUN and include complete Appendices A–E. Their text, figures, tables, algorithms and proofs can be matched despite the changed title and formatting.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original accuracy, runtime, unlearning-efficacy and sensitivity experiments on six graph datasets.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain these original experiments, including billion-edge graph evaluation, Deleted Data Replay Tests and membership inference attacks.

M1.justification: The lazy local propagation procedure, approximate-embedding Newton update, perturbation objective and retraining trigger are unchanged. Algorithms 1–4 retain the same steps.

E1.justification: Both evaluate Cora, Citeseer, Photo, ogbn-arxiv, ogbn-products and ogbn-papers100M under the same removal and adversarial scenarios. The node/feature and replay-test experiments emphasized in v2 already appear in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain the same participants: CGU, CEU and retraining where applicable. The replay test retains Origin, Retrain, CGU and ScaleGUN; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: For the ogbn-papers100M node/feature experiments, v2 Section 5 corrects v1 Appendix C.2's description of '2000 edges' per batch to '2000 nodes.' The corresponding table is unchanged, indicating a description correction rather than evidence of rerunning. Other splits, metrics, configurations and removal schedules match.

E4.justification: The gradient-bound validation, approximation-threshold, noise, batch-size and large-removal analyses are retained, as are adversarial-edge tests, DDRT and MIA. Moving DDRT into the main text adds no analysis.

E5.justification: V2 Table 4 removes six reported uncertainty terms from v1 Table 12, including ScaleGUN's 0.08 ± 0.01 and Origin's 45.59 ± 13.90. Both versions still specify five trials with random seeds and retain uncertainty in MIA Table 13; no change in run count is established.

E6.justification: All fourteen matched tables retain their central numerical values, and all six figures retain their plotted results. V1 Tables 9 and 12 become v2 Tables 2 and 4 without new result entries; the uncertainty omissions are assessed under E5.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, propagation invariants, complexity bounds and certified-unlearning bounds are unchanged. Appendix E's proofs match apart from citation formatting and reflow.

C1.justification: Both claim the first certified graph-unlearning approach scaling to billion-edge graphs, certification for three removal scenarios and efficient propagation updates. V2 foregrounds the approximation-error barrier without changing these contributions or guarantees.

C2.justification: The approximation/privacy/retraining tradeoffs, degree-based explanations and limitations of certification for nonlinear models are retained. V2's main-text caution about MIA restates the mismatch already discussed in v1 Appendix C.4.

D1.justification: Hardware, 40-thread computation, hyperparameter tables, data-selection instructions, dataset licenses and code-access information are retained. The common symmetric propagation matrix moves from Appendix C.1 into Section 5 rather than being newly disclosed.

R1.justification: The introduction adds application and privacy references, including LightGCN, DeepInf, financial-network work and a graph-unlearning survey, while removing several sampling and historical-embedding citations. Positioning relative to CGU, CEU and InstantGNN and the substantive Appendix A discussion remain stable.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and extensively rewrites the abstract, introductory motivation and contribution narrative. It reorganizes the experimental exposition to foreground node/feature results and distinguish edge from node efficacy, and removes the separate Broader Impact paragraph.

P2.justification: The title block, headings and page styling change, and Figure 1 gains panel labels. Two existing appendix tables move into the main text, with accompanying renumbering and resizing; the plots and basic table designs remain intact.

improvement.justification: V2 explains the approximation-versus-certification obstacle more clearly and integrates existing node/feature and replay-test evidence into the main argument. These improve accessibility, although removing DDRT uncertainty weakens statistical transparency. With the method, proofs and central results unchanged, the net improvement is limited.
